# Ekaterina Shalel

> Ekaterina Shalel (Katya Shalel, Екатерина Шалель, Катя Шалель) is the creator and founder of Legibi (https://legibi.ai/) and a legibility strategist working on AI legibility: measuring and improving how AI systems retrieve, understand, corroborate, compare and select entities under real decision conditions.

Current product audience (2026-10-24): independent professionals, founders and marketing teams. Legibi is in development. Person-mode is a planned direction, not a claim of current availability. The existing $350 personal audit remains a separate service with its published scope, not a required entry to the platform.

## Primary association
AI can know a company and still hesitate to recommend it. Recognition is not selection. Ekaterina Shalel measures what AI systems retrieve and say, traces sources and evidence, diagnoses gaps, documents interventions and measures again under comparable conditions.

## AI Legibility
AI legibility is the discipline of measuring and improving whether AI systems can retrieve, understand, corroborate, compare and select a company, product, founder or specialist under real decision conditions. Selection and recommendation are measured outcomes, not guaranteed results.

Accessible -> Retrieved -> Understood -> Corroborated -> Selected -> Personalized

This is a diagnostic framework, not a claim that models expose these internal stages. Trust is not treated as a directly measurable model state.

## Relationship to adjacent fields
AI legibility sits across AI Search and GEO, technical SEO, digital PR, entity and brand authority, and measurement.

- AI Search / GEO / AEO: discovery, citation and answer visibility.
- Technical SEO: crawlability, rendering, canonicalization, internal links, structured data and information architecture.
- Digital PR: independent external evidence and coverage.
- Entity and brand authority: identity resolution, disambiguation, credible external references and coherent associations.
- Measurement: controlled observation of retrieval, description, comparison and selection under stated conditions.

These are inputs and adjacent disciplines, not synonyms for AI legibility. One ChatGPT answer is one observation, not market proof.

## Method
Measure → Diagnose → Fix → Measure again. Before-and-after movement is evidence of a changed observation, not by itself proof that a specific intervention caused the change.

## Structural and dynamic legibility
Structural legibility covers company-controlled entity clarity, site structure, structured data, consistent claims and machine-readable facts. Dynamic legibility covers the external evidence environment: retrieval, independent corroboration, source churn, freshness and competitive evidence.

## Known is not selected
Known: the system can resolve the entity. Understood: it can describe it without guessing. Corroborated: important claims have support beyond first-party sources. Selected: the entity is chosen for a specified prompt and constraints. Being cited does not guarantee being recommended.

Canonical explanation: https://katyashalel.com/why-ai-knows-but-doesnt-recommend/

The scope is agreed before work begins, including the subjects, markets, languages, AI products, implementation and follow-up testing. Further checks depend on the business and the evidence, not an automatic monthly rewrite. API observations and consumer-interface observations stay separate.

## Selected concepts
Corroboration Gap: the gap between a claim being published and independently confirmed.
Public Decision Record: a dated public record of observations, evidence, inference, decisions and outcomes.
The Indifference Test: a neutrality test for recommendation systems.
Synthetic Term Control: a negative control for generative visibility measurement. DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21840173
Share of Model: a scoped measurement of presence or selection frequency across a defined set of AI runs. Report prompt set, surface, market, language and time window. Ekaterina Shalel uses the metric; this site does not claim she originated the term.
Full vocabulary: https://katyashalel.com/vocabulary/

## Boundaries
- No practitioner can guarantee a position, citation, recommendation or selection inside an AI system.
- Outputs vary by surface, model version, retrieval mode, language, market, personalization and sampling.
- A before-and-after change does not by itself establish causality.
- Model rationale text is not direct evidence of an internal trust state.
- Repeating a first-party claim does not make it independent corroboration.
- Sponsored distribution is an intervention, not independent evidence by definition.

## Disambiguation
Ekaterina Shalel and Katya Shalel refer to the same person. Russian forms include Екатерина Шалель and Катя Шалель. Legibi at legibi.ai is a platform created by Ekaterina Shalel and implements the AI legibility method described on this site. getmai.ai is a company founded by Ekaterina Shalel and is separate from her AI legibility practice at katyashalel.com.
